## 2026-09-29 — P0 "logged-in users cannot play online": standard vs hard
Context: fullstack P0 card, no override, one-line spec ("can't start or join online matches"), root
cause unknown. The relay has no auth of its own: `MultiplayerContext` emits `identify { user }` with
the Redux user before `findMatch`/`createFriendRoom`/join, and `multiplayer_server/src/index.js`
keys players by `user.id || user.username`, dropping the socket silently when neither exists. So the
likely suspects are the logged-in user payload (recent `hydrateSession`/cached `/me/` and
`token/refresh/` user changes from 2026-09-23, or the inlined `profile_photo` data URL) or the
identify handshake itself. `hard` was defensible (the rubric lists anything touching the multiplayer
protocol); `standard` was defensible because the fix is most likely a bounded payload/handshake
repair in an existing pattern, not a new protocol or state machine.
Decision: `difficulty: standard` (bias small; the failure policy escalates), `risk: high` (the fix
lands on session/user-payload code or the relay `identify` handshake), `needsDesignRound: true`
(multi-area: frontend + backend + multiplayer + auth; verifying needs the relay running with two
logged-in users), `engineModel: opus` (non-trivial P0 and risk high override), `planModel: fable`.
Consequences: the design round's first job is a reproduction and a named root cause before any plan
step; if it proves to be a new protocol shape rather than a payload fix, the round should re-rate it
`hard`. Guests vs logged-in is the key contrast — the plan must keep guest play working.
"
}
